$comment: Recorded pack sizes, refreshed 2026-09-14 and the refresh is the story. `check:artifacts` existed, `artifact-size-ratchet-lock.test.ts` unit-tested its verdict function against synthetic inputs, and **no workflow ever ran the verdict against the real packages** — so seven of them drifted past this file unchallenged: closeout +268%, seniority +112%, paratext +87%, burgee +51%, caique +46%, flagstaff +15%, linegauge +11%. The growth is explained — the PLAN 1.1 schema fold put a 6.5 KB family schema in every package that reaches the plugin registry, and waves 1 and 3 added plugin hosts and drop-in façades — but explaining growth is not the same as accepting it, which is why the numbers are named here rather than quietly replaced. `npm run lint` runs the check now, so the next one is caught. seniority moved 2026-09-20, deliberately and in one direction: 47,616 -> 59,124 gzipped and 153,040 -> 193,682 unpacked, +24.2% and +26.6%. The cause is two drop-in subpaths that did not exist — `seniority/lilconfig` (lilconfig 3.1.3's surface, which took its compat row from 0 / 77 to 67 / 77) and `seniority/rc` (rc 1.2.8's merge without its four dependencies). Both are product, not drift, and the package's own R9 ceiling in `shape.test.ts` — 140,000 B of built `dist`, measured against lilconfig — is still met. The band is raised here rather than the ceiling there, because they measure different things: this one is the tarball a consumer downloads, that one is the graph a bundler walks. **Lowered 2026-09-21, and this direction needs no permission.** `scripts/strip-comments.mjs` read only the top level of `dist/`, so every nested entry point shipped its doc comments: burgee unpacked 949,221 -> 635,640 (-33.0%) and flagstaff 200,204 -> 188,624 the moment it recursed. A ratchet tightening is always free; it is the loosening that is a decision. **2026-09-21: `linegauge` and `seniority` were the two published packages whose build never ran `strip-comments` at all** — not a recursion gap, simply absent from their `build` script. Adding it: linegauge unpacked 83,538 -> 56,148 (-32.8%), seniority 193,682 -> 139,793 (-27.8%). Both directions of this file's history now have the same cause: a stripper that was not reaching what it was supposed to reach. **Raised 2026-09-23, burgee only: 173,668 -> 189,725 gzipped and 677,098 -> 744,915 unpacked (+9.2%, +10.0%).** The cause is the façades' type surface: `burgee/yargs` shipped no `Argv`, `Arguments` or `CommandModule`, so every TypeScript + yargs adoption target failed to compile after `burgee migrate`. `dist/yargs/types.d.ts` is @types/yargs' declarations with their doc comments — 53,093 bytes, the hover text a yargs user already reads — and emits 11 bytes of JavaScript, so no bundle and no import graph moved; the rest is `migrate`'s export table and name check. Declarations keep their comments by the same rule as every other `.d.ts` here (`strip-comments.mjs`). **Raised 2026-09-23, paratext only: 29,566 -> 32,593 gzipped and 92,160 -> 101,438 unpacked (+10.2%, +10.1%).** The cause is A27: `paratext/terminal-link` now carries `supports-hyperlinks` 4.5.0's own detection (`dist/hyperlinks.js`) instead of paratext's `LINK.when`, which disagreed with the incumbent in 30 of 55 environments graded in `hyperlinks.test.ts`. That table is what makes the row level and lets `burgee migrate` rewrite `terminal-link`; the root entry does not import it. **Raised 2026-09-27, closeout only: 31,178 -> 35,140 gzipped and 95,387 -> 109,473 unpacked (+12.7%, +14.8%).** Main already stood at 103,646 unpacked (+8.7%, inside the allowance) from growth since 2026-09-14; this change adds 5,827 B for design R4, which was one third built: `alternateScreen()` and `rawMode()` paired with their undos in the restore phase, the registry finishing the phases a drained event loop left behind, their declarations (doc comments kept, by the `.d.ts` rule above), and the README documenting them. Product, not drift; `weight.test.ts` holds the per-entry budgets and D-163 records the design. **Raised 2026-09-27, linegauge only: 26,717 -> 29,604 gzipped and 83,683 -> 95,160 unpacked (+10.8%, +13.7%).** Main stood at 27,605 / 86,464 just before #655 (+3.3% on both, inside the allowance); #655 adds 1,999 B gzipped and 8,696 B unpacked, and `dist/slice.js` is 7,580 B of it (2,108 -> 9,688): `slice.ts` rewritten over slice-ansi 9.0.1's token grammar and walk, which took `linegauge/slice` from 53 / 104 to 104 / 104, level with the control. The WIDE table generated from get-east-asian-width 1.7.0 (Unicode 17, 122 -> 126 ranges, the 1,147 code points the hand-written one lacked) costs 76 B of `dist/width.js`. Product, not drift; `ceilings.json` holds the per-entry budgets, and #655 moved `linegauge/slice`'s there.caique only: 39,267 -> 62,116 gzipped and 121,782 -> 210,330 unpacked (+58.2%, +72.7%).** The cause is D-152: `caique/clack` was `limitOptions` alone and now carries `@clack/prompts`' twelve prompts, its writers, glyphs and settings on caique's own keypress loop, which is what took clack's graded row from 14 / 17 to 16 / 17. Product, not drift: `./clack`'s static graph is 62,238 B against clack's 101,684 B across six packages (`caique/src/weight.test.ts`), about a third of the unpacked growth is the new `.d.ts` files with their doc comments, and a program that imports caique's own API reaches none of it. **Raised 2026-09-27, all nine: the package READMEs.** Every README ships in its tarball, and each now carries the family header — tagline, the eleven-badge row and a compatibility badge per graded suite — plus Install, Migrating, For agents and the generated family table, Contributing and Licence sections (`scripts/readme-benchmarks.ts`, held by `package-readme-header-lock.test.ts`). No package source moved on that branch, so no bundle or import graph did either. Unpacked, measured after merging main at cbe720da91 (so closeout's R4 and linegauge's slice-ansi 9 source are in the figure too): burgee 808,874 -> 824,250; caique 121,782 -> 130,540 (210,330 on main after #638, whose paragraph this follows; 63,921 / 217,148 with these READMEs on top, measured after merging main at e4c1f6951d); flagstaff 201,484 -> 211,252; roundel 77,346 -> 84,841; bellpull 97,040 -> 111,586; closeout 109,473 -> 117,538; linegauge 83,683 -> 102,495 (95,160 on main after #676, which this paragraph follows); seniority 151,463 -> 164,456; paratext 101,438 -> 114,845. Where that exceeds the README's own growth, the difference is drift under the 10% allowance that had already accumulated since the last raise, and linegauge's new slice and width-table source from #655, absorbed here rather than left to trip the next unrelated change. Re-measured after merging main at 12fea8eae4: every figure above holds exactly except burgee (828,206) and flagstaff (211,355), which #665's parser and cli-table3 source moved on main by less than 0.5%; they keep this branch's figures, inside the allowance, rather than being raised for code this branch did not write. **Raised 2026-09-28, controlroom only: 3,357 -> 5,264 gzipped and 7,109 -> 13,384 unpacked.** The cause is its README, which is most of a reserved package's tarball: it now carries the family header (tagline, the badge row with `status: reserved` in the coverage slot), Install, Quick start, the planned Migrating and For agents sections, and the generated family table, Contributing and Licence. The one exported constant did not move. The other nine grew by the table's new controlroom row, inside the allowance. **Raised 2026-09-30, roundel only: 29,804 -> 35,692 gzipped and 84,841 -> 102,435 unpacked (+19.8%, +20.7%).** The cause is R11, `roundel/import`: `dist/import.js` 6,438 B and `dist/import.d.ts` 5,039 B (its doc comments kept, by the `.d.ts` rule above), the README's section on it (+1,681 B) and the `./import` export (+134 B) — 13,292 B of the growth. The other 4,302 B is drift on main since the last raise, under the 10% allowance, absorbed here rather than left to trip the next unrelated change. Product, not drift: `weight.test.ts` holds `./import` to 16,600 B of reachable `dist`, and a program that does not import it reaches none of it. **Raised 2026-09-30, seniority only: 46,911 -> 54,424 gzipped and 164,456 -> 193,213 unpacked (+16.0%, +17.5%).** The cause is `seniority/yaml` (D-20260930-seniority-yaml): `dist/yaml.js` 24,226 B and `dist/yaml.d.ts` 2,440 B, the README's section on reading YAML (+623 B) and the `./yaml` export — 27,419 B of the 28,757. The other 1,338 B is drift on main since the last raise, under the 10% allowance. Product, not drift: it is the parser that takes cosmiconfig's row from 186 / 243 to 240 / 243, level with the control, and `shape.test.ts` holds `dist/yaml.js` to 25,000 B and asserts no other built module imports it, so a program that reads no YAML reaches none of it. controlroom moved 2026-10-06, deliberately: 63,792 -> 82,048 gzipped and 238,157 -> 329,856 unpacked, +28.6% and +38.5%. The cause is `controlroom/ink` following ink 8.0.0 (D-20261006-controlroom-ink-8) — a suite that grew from 593 cases to 1,309, four new hooks, the alternate screen and the rest of yoga that ink 8 sets — and the subpath is still under ink 8.0.0's own `build/` of 250,669 B before yoga.
